name: Rocket Dart
author: whirligig
notes: A fin-stabilised rocket dart on a solid motor: 1.1 kg on the pad, 420 g of which is propellant that leaves in two and a half seconds. Everything interesting here is in the mass. The rocket gets lighter as it burns, so its acceleration climbs even though the thrust is constant; the centre of gravity walks forward as the propellant at the back disappears, which is why the fins get MORE effective as the burn goes on; and because the thrust is specified against a sea-level specific impulse, the motor gains a little as it climbs out of the air that was pushing back on its nozzle. A solid motor cannot be throttled and cannot be shut down once lit, and the model refuses to pretend otherwise — `throttleable` is false, so the throttle channel is an igniter, not a lever. Datum is the nose.
